We actually had a fantastic dinner here - despite the many low ratings
Oct 2025 • Couples
Walked by this restaurant a few times. Always looked busy, fun and good. And it was only a few minutes away by foot from our Hotel.
So the last night we decided to get some dinner here. We did read the reviews and knew about the issues some customers adressed (rude service, close to being racist). That said, I visited with my Asian wife, maybe that made our experience better and easier.

We actually wanted a table outside, but they were all reserved - and yes, they actually were and the restaurant was completely packed 30min later. But we got a good table inside. A good choice, because an hour later it was pouring outside and everybody (including thet tables) had to move inside.

Staff was actually fine, not overly friendly, but in no ways rude. And food and drinks arrived fast. And the food served here is excellent!

They have a huge menu with all the vietnamese classics. But a lot more than that! Lots of rare dishes and items as well. Definitely worth trying something a bit new here.

We ordered some fried rice, snails, deep-fried eel, chicken feet, duck tongue with holy basil and stuffed small squid.

The dishes were freshly cooked, deep-fried items nice and crispy. All dishes were fantastic, but some did stand out: The eel was divine and the squid excellent as well. Cooked to perfection. But really, everything was nicely done. Really fresh, greatly cooked authentic food here.

And there were lots of more interesting things that we couldn't try this time: Oyster, blood cockels, whole fish, deep-fried crab and more. Surely a place we will come back to next time. Prices were fair for the quality served.

A fun place with a nice, relaxed and lively atmosphere. Good food, cold beer. Everybody had fun. So did we.

Friendly local restaurant!
May 2018 • Friends
Strongly recommend this restaurant for foreign tourists and Vietnamese who gonna travel to Saigon. Let’s us tell you some reasons why we normally choose Vy Da Quan for our meeting place:
- Location: Located on the corner of Ly Tu Trong street and Nguyen Trung Truc street, Vy Da Quan is close to many tourist attractions, malls, hotels and offices. Is it a good sound if sitting down here for couple of beers after long time outside? - Good point
- Staffs: There aren’t no words to explain how friendly and helpful they were with us. They were very attentive on the guests’ demanding/ quickly on serving and cleaning. - Good point
- Quality: You get what you pay for. Vy Da Quan isn’t exceptional. Compared with the other restaurants in Saigon, this place seems to be a little bit more expensive but they have been serving by fresh and best ingredients. The easiest way to double check is to order the seafood dishes. If you were born and grew up in the agriculture country, it isn’t difficult to recognize the ingredients fresh or not. 
Highly recommend this place!

Great restaurant, good food
Nov 2014 • Family
This restaurant is on a corner and can easily be seen from the main junction. The restaurant serves Vietnamese food / dishes and also some BBQ dishes. 

There seems to be a large selection of beers for the thirsty traveler, but limited choice for those who don't drink beer. They also automatically swap your block of ice out of your beer for a fresh block of ice (this takes some getting used to, but when in Rome!). We were lucky that the person serving us graciously offered to get us some tasty Vietnamese iced coffee from the other restaurant, now that's service!

Their BBQ dishes are very tasty, and we were recommended a few dishes (like the BBQ prawns in chilli etc) that were amazing. One thing to take note, if you want to have a big fish dish (BBQ), it might take a bit of time (about 30 - 40 minutes depending on the size of the fish) - the restaurant owner suggested to get the hotel to call them so they can start preparing. But this is pretty much worth the wait.

One issue would be the constant street peddlers that come up to your table to sell you stuff, but this is part of the charm of eating out in Vietnam. 

Do take note that the chairs and tables are pretty low, so it would be a problem for taller people or for those with knee issues (seems to be a general Vietnam thing in most restaurants).

The owner's daughter spoke excellent English, apologised for the delay in food and even offered us complimentary sliced guava as a desert.

Fantastic food - deserves more attention!
Jul 2014 • Couples
We stayed near this restaurant and took the busyness as a very good sign - and we were right! Tables and chairs are out on the street as is fairly typical, and although they were all busy when we arrived, another table and two chairs were magicked up for us! We had a seafood rice, beef noodles, morning glory with garlic and enjoyed every bite! Whilst there was frog and plenty of other seafood choices ie clams etc on the menu, we didn't try these. Other people had table top stoves to cook some of their own items - not sure what you needed to order to get one of these, but they looked very interesting! Service was quick but very pleasant, and portion size good. As soon as my husband's beer was finished, there was another one being offered promptly! We would definitely have eaten here again, but the choice of places in the area is vast - definitely worth a visit if you are looking for good food at a very reasonable price.
